result: Targeted Biocrates CSF metabolomics/lipidomics in separate non-exercise and post-submaximal-exercise lumbar puncture cohorts found raised serine, sarcosine and phospholipids with lower 5MTHF in ME/CFS; after exercise lipids were consumed in both groups while metabolites were consumed in ME/CFS but generated in controls.

result: In 83 CFS patients vs 83 controls on a 2-to-1 Stroop task, larger raw Stroop interference was fully explained by generally slower processing speed; z-scored RTs showed no attentional selectivity deficit, with strong Bayesian evidence for the null.
reason: same domain and measure (RT/processing speed); adds that the deficit is slowed processing rather than impaired selective attention

result: In 948 menstruating Visible app users with long COVID and/or ME/CFS, symptoms were worst during menstruation (early luteal IRR 0.963 vs menstrual), crashes were more frequent during menstruation, and combined hormonal contraception users (n=70) had lower symptom scores (OR 0.83) and fewer crashes (OR 0.55) than non-users (n=786).
reason: menstrual-cycle symptom modulation is covered by the existing endocrine-menstrual-cycle finding; adds crash timing and contraception data

result: In a German population-based nested case-control study (982 PCS, 576 controls), 67.6% of PCS cases persisted into year two; persistent PCS had lower VO2max (27.9 vs 31.0 ml/kg/min), handgrip (40.2 vs 42.5 kg) and higher VE/VCO2 slope than recovered controls, with no lab, cardiac, EBV or viral-persistence differences; 35.6% reported PEM >14 h and 11.6% ME/CFS-compatible symptoms.
reason: does not measure IOM/CCC ME/CFS incidence or ME/CFS-subgroup course; its objective result is lower peak VO2 in persistent PCS vs recovered controls, plus PEM prevalence

result: In 94 long COVID patients (40 IOH, 29 POTS, 25 normal) vs 33 controls on 10-min active stand, long COVID had lower upright HF-HRV (p=0.04) and LF BP variability (p=0.001); IOH had lower supine baroreflex sensitivity and POTS lower upright sympathetic/parasympathetic modulation.
reason: same group/network as cited Hira 2023 (CanLoCAN), likely overlapping cohort; adds HRV/BRS mechanism by orthostatic phenotype rather than independently replicating

result: Long COVID patients (n=94) had lower upright high-frequency HRV (p=0.04) than 33 healthy controls during active stand, with lowest values in the POTS subgroup.
reason: same measure (HF-HRV) and direction but in long COVID, not ME/CFS: a long COVID extension, not a replication

result: [18F]-FEPPA TSPO PET with arterial input and genotype adjustment in 14 N-PASC vs 10 never-COVID essential workers found higher hippocampal VT in persistent brain fog (AUC 0.95; sensitivity/specificity 0.88/0.93).
reason: independent cohort, TSPO PET, raised signal in long COVID, supporting the positive side of the contested finding

result: 7T MRI with FreeSurfer subfield segmentation found larger left hippocampal head subfield volumes (subiculum, presubiculum, molecular layer, whole head; p 0.002-0.014) in 29 ME/CFS and 17 long COVID vs 15 controls, associated with severity measures.
reason: tests regional grey-matter volume and reports a difference, against the finding's null claim; small single-group study, so weak evidence

result: In 45 PCS (26 with ME/CFS), 36 post-infectious ME/CFS and 34 controls, IgG to poly-R peptides of SRRM3, SLC24A3, TSPYL2, TSPYL5 and to full-length alpha-adrenergic receptors was more frequent in patients and associated with autonomic, fatigue, cognitive and pain symptoms.
reason: measures alpha-adrenergic and EBV-mimic poly-R autoantibodies, not beta2/M3/M4 GPCR antibodies; the fitting finding (immune-neural-autoantibodies) already cites its published version (Hoheisel 2025, Front Immunol)
